response: No, arterial line sampling is not reliable for performing activated plasma thromboplastin time (aPTT) after cardiac surgery. This is because the heparinized solution used to flush and maintain the patency of the arterial line can interfere with the aPTT results, leading to inaccurate and potentially misleading values. It is recommended to use peripheral venous samples for coagulation studies, including aPTT, to ensure accurate results and guide clinical decision-making.
